raw_text: FIR No. 001/2024 dated 15-01-2024. PS Hazratganj, District Lucknow. Complainant: Shri Rajesh Kumar Sharma, age 45 years, S/o Late Shri Hari Prasad Sharma, R/o 24/A Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. The complainant states that on 14-01-2024 at approximately 2230 hours, while returning home from his shop at Aminabad Market, near the Charbagh underpass, two unknown persons on a black Pulsar motorcycle (no number plate visible) intercepted him. One accused, approximately 25 years old, medium build, wearing a black hoodie, put a knife to his throat while the second person, approximately 22 years old, slim build, wearing jeans and red jacket, snatched his gold chain (approx 25 grams, value Rs. 1,25,000), mobile phone (Samsung Galaxy S23, IMEI: 354789102345678), and wallet containing Rs. 15,000 cash and ATM cards. The accused persons fled towards Charbagh railway station. The complainant sustained minor injuries on neck. One passerby identified the knife-wielding accused as 'Bablu' who is known in the Charbagh area for chain snatching. Sections: 392, 397 IPC. Investigation handed to SI Arun Verma.

FIR No. 002/2024 dated 22-01-2024. PS Charbagh, District Lucknow. Complainant: Smt. Priya Tiwari, age 32 years, W/o Shri Amit Tiwari, R/o 56 Alambagh Colony, Lucknow. The complainant states that on 21-01-2024 at about 2100 hours, near Charbagh railway station foot overbridge, she was walking towards the auto stand when one person on a motorcycle grabbed her purse and dragged her for approximately 10 meters. Purse contained Rs. 8,000 cash, gold earrings (15 grams, value Rs. 75,000), Aadhaar card, and iPhone 14 (IMEI: 891234567890123). Accused was identified by a nearby vendor as Bablu alias Bhura, age approximately 25 years, resident of Thakurganj area, who operates with an accomplice named Sunny. Accused was wearing black hoodie and riding a Pulsar motorcycle without number plate. Complainant suffered abrasions on left arm and knee. Sections: 392, 356 IPC. CCTV footage from railway station being obtained.

FIR No. 003/2024 dated 03-02-2024. PS Kotwali Nagar, District Kanpur. Complainant: Shri Mohammad Irfan, age 55 years, S/o Late Shri Mohammad Yusuf, R/o Collectorganj, Kanpur. The complainant reports that between 02-02-2024 2300 hours and 03-02-2024 0400 hours, unknown persons broke into his electronics shop 'Irfan Electronics' at Collectorganj market by cutting the lock with a gas cutter. Stolen property includes: 15 Samsung smartphones (total value Rs. 4,50,000), 8 laptops of various brands (total value Rs. 5,60,000), cash from counter drawer Rs. 45,000, and CCTV DVR unit. Total loss approximately Rs. 10,55,000. Preliminary investigation reveals the lock was cut with a portable gas cutter, and the rear wall had tool marks suggesting professional burglars. Neighboring shopkeepers reported seeing a white Maruti Eeco van (partial plate UP-78 XXXX) parked behind the market between 0100-0300 hours. Sections: 457, 380 IPC. Fingerprint team deployed.

FIR No. 004/2024 dated 10-02-2024. PS Swaroop Nagar, District Kanpur. Complainant: Shri Anil Kumar Gupta, age 48 years, S/o Shri Ram Naresh Gupta, R/o Kakadeo, Kanpur. The complainant reports that on 09-02-2024 night, his garment shop 'Gupta Garments' at Swaroop Nagar market was burgled. Entry was made by cutting the rear shutter with a gas cutter. Property stolen: 200+ branded garments (value Rs. 8,00,000), cash Rs. 65,000 from the safe, and gold jewelry kept in shop locker (120 grams, value Rs. 6,00,000). Total estimated loss Rs. 14,65,000. Similar modus operandi as recent burglaries in Collectorganj — gas cutter used on metal lock/shutter, CCTV DVR taken, occurred in early morning hours. A white Eeco van was reportedly seen by the night watchman at approximately 0200 hours. The accused appear to be an organized gang targeting commercial establishments. Sections: 457, 380, 411 IPC. Investigation reveals possible connection to FIR/2024/KN/003.

FIR No. 005/2024 dated 18-02-2024. PS Civil Lines, District Agra. Complainant: Smt. Sunita Devi, age 60 years, W/o Late Shri Mohan Lal, R/o Sadar Bazaar, Agra. The complainant states that she received a phone call from a person claiming to be from State Bank of India, identifying himself as 'Vikram Sharma from SBI customer care'. He informed her that her KYC was expiring and her account would be blocked. Under pressure, she shared her Aadhaar number, debit card details, and OTP received on her phone. Subsequently, Rs. 4,85,000 was debited from her SBI account in 6 transactions over 30 minutes. The amount was transferred to multiple accounts. Cyber cell investigation revealed the phone number (+91-9876543210) was registered on a fake ID. The money trail leads to accounts in Jamtara, Jharkhand — a known hub for cyber fraud operations. Accused persons identified as members of a Jamtara-based cyber fraud ring. Sections: 420, 66C, 66D IT Act 2000. Case referred to Cyber Crime PS.

FIR No. 006/2024 dated 25-02-2024. PS Tajganj, District Agra. Complainant: Shri Devendra Singh, age 35 years, S/o Shri Bhagwan Singh, R/o Fatehpur Sikri Road, Agra. Complainant reports that his 14-year-old daughter Pooja (name changed) did not return home from school on 24-02-2024. She was last seen leaving Govt. Girls Inter College, Tajganj at 1400 hours. Complainant suspects one Raju alias Chhotu, age approximately 22 years, S/o unknown, resident of Lohamandi area, who had been seen loitering near the school and had been sending messages to the victim through social media. Victim's phone is switched off (IMEI: 567890123456789). Raju has a prior case of eve-teasing registered at Tajganj PS in 2023. Neighbors confirm seeing Raju on a red Honda Activa near the school gate around 1345 hours on 24-02-2024. Sections: 363, 366 IPC, Sec 8/12 POCSO Act. Immediate search operation initiated.

FIR No. 007/2024 dated 05-03-2024. PS Lanka, District Varanasi. Complainant: Shri Ramesh Chandra Pandey, age 52 years, S/o Late Shri Kailash Nath Pandey, R/o Assi Ghat area, Varanasi. The complainant reports a case of extortion. On 04-03-2024, he received threatening calls from an unknown number demanding Rs. 10,00,000 'protection money' for his restaurant 'Pandey Ji Ka Dhaba' near Assi Ghat. Caller identified himself as working for 'Munna Bhai' and threatened to burn down the restaurant if payment was not made within 48 hours. Similar threatening calls were received by three other shopkeepers in the Assi Ghat area — Shri Vinod Kashyap (sweet shop), Shri Akhilesh Yadav (cloth shop), and Smt. Meera Sahu (general store). All four victims received calls from different numbers but the caller referred to the same 'Munna Bhai'. This appears to be an organized extortion racket targeting businesses in the tourist area. Sections: 384, 506, 120B IPC. Phone numbers being traced.

FIR No. 008/2024 dated 12-03-2024. PS Bhelupur, District Varanasi. Complainant: Station House Officer, Bhelupur PS (suo motu). During a routine patrol on 11-03-2024 at approximately 2300 hours near Godowlia Chowk, police team led by SI Manoj Kumar intercepted a suspicious Alto car (UP-65 AB 1234). Upon search, recovered 2.5 kg ganja and 50 grams of brown sugar (heroin) concealed in a modified compartment under the rear seat. Accused persons arrested: (1) Guddu alias Guddu Khan, age 28, S/o Shri Naseem Khan, R/o Madanpura, Varanasi — the driver, (2) Pappu alias Pappu Yadav, age 24, S/o Shri Shivnath Yadav, R/o Ramnagar, Varanasi — the carrier. Both accused have prior NDPS cases. Guddu has 3 previous cases at various PS in Varanasi district. Investigation reveals they are part of a supply chain operating from the Nepal border through Gorakhpur to Varanasi. Sections: 20, 21, 22 NDPS Act. Accused produced before NDPS court.

FIR No. 009/2024 dated 20-03-2024. PS Rapti Nagar, District Gorakhpur. Complainant: Shri Santosh Kumar Mishra, age 40 years, S/o Shri Brijmohan Mishra, R/o Medical College Road, Gorakhpur. The complainant reports that on 19-03-2024 at approximately 1830 hours, while he was closing his medical store, three persons armed with country-made pistols entered the shop and demanded cash and medicines. Accused persons took Rs. 2,20,000 cash, and medicines including scheduled drugs (Tramadol, Codeine-based cough syrups, Alprazolam) worth Rs. 1,50,000. The main accused was identified as Chhote Lal alias Chhotu, age approximately 30 years, with a scar on his left cheek, who is a known criminal in the area with prior cases of robbery and arms act violations. Two accomplices were unidentified. They fled on two motorcycles towards Sahjanwa road. Sections: 392, 397, 25 Arms Act. Multiple teams deployed for arrest.

FIR No. 010/2024 dated 28-03-2024. PS Kotwali, District Gorakhpur. Complainant: Shri Hari Om Agrawal, age 62 years, S/o Late Shri Jagdish Prasad Agrawal, R/o Golghar, Gorakhpur. The complainant reports a case of financial fraud. Between January 2024 and March 2024, he was approached by one Vikram Sharma (claimed to be a SEBI-registered investment advisor) through WhatsApp, who promised 200% returns on cryptocurrency investment. Complainant invested Rs. 15,00,000 in multiple installments through UPI transfers. Initially received Rs. 50,000 as 'returns' to build trust. Subsequently, when he tried to withdraw, the accused demanded 'tax payment' of Rs. 3,00,000. Total loss: Rs. 18,00,000. Investigation reveals 'Vikram Sharma' is an alias used by a Jamtara-based cyber fraud network. Same alias and modus operandi reported in Agra (FIR/2024/AG/005) and other UP districts. Sections: 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, 66C, 66D IT Act. Coordinated investigation with Cyber Crime PS.

FIR No. 011/2024 dated 05-04-2024. PS Gomti Nagar, District Lucknow. Complainant: Dr. Neha Agarwal, age 38 years, D/o Shri P.K. Agarwal, R/o Vikas Nagar, Lucknow. Complainant reports a case of cyberstalking and identity theft. An unknown person created fake social media profiles using her photographs and personal information, posted defamatory content, and sent threatening messages to her colleagues and patients. Investigation traced the IP addresses to Kanpur. The accused has been identified as Rohit Mishra, age 27, R/o Kidwai Nagar, Kanpur, a former employee of complainant's clinic who was terminated 6 months ago. Accused had saved complainant's personal photos and data during employment. Accused also created a fake matrimonial profile of the complainant on multiple platforms. Sections: 354D, 500, 509 IPC, 66C, 66E, 67 IT Act 2000. Cyber forensics team extracting digital evidence from seized devices.

FIR No. 012/2024 dated 12-04-2024. PS Civil Lines, District Prayagraj. Complainant: Shri Arvind Kumar Singh, age 55 years, S/o Shri Raghunath Singh, R/o George Town, Prayagraj. The complainant reports that on 11-04-2024 at approximately 2100 hours, his son Aditya Singh (age 24) was assaulted by a group of 5-6 persons near Sangam area. The accused persons, identified as members of the Munna Bhai gang, attacked with iron rods and hockey sticks after the victim refused to pay 'protection money' for his newly opened gym. The victim sustained fractures to his left arm and multiple lacerations. Accused identified: (1) Rinku alias Rinku Pandey, age 26, (2) Sonu Tiwari, age 23, (3) 3-4 others unidentified. The gang is reportedly operating an extortion racket across Prayagraj and Varanasi, demanding money from new businesses. Similar extortion cases reported at Lanka PS, Varanasi. Sections: 307, 384, 506, 120B, 148, 149 IPC. Victim hospitalized at SRN Hospital.

FIR No. 013/2024 dated 20-04-2024. PS Hazratganj, District Lucknow. Complainant: Shri Manoj Kumar Verma, age 42 years, S/o Shri Deen Dayal Verma, R/o Indira Nagar, Lucknow. The complainant reports that on 19-04-2024 at approximately 2345 hours, while returning from a family function, near Lalbagh area, his car was stopped by two persons on a black motorcycle. One accused put a knife to his throat and the second snatched his Rolex watch (value Rs. 8,50,000), gold ring (20 grams), wallet with Rs. 25,000 cash, and car keys. The accused then drove away his Hyundai Creta (UP-32 AB 5678). A witness identified one accused as 'Bablu' who is notorious for vehicle lifting and chain snatching in the Hazratganj-Charbagh corridor. The accused matches the description from FIR/2024/LC/001 and FIR/2024/LC/002 — black hoodie, Pulsar motorcycle, knife-wielding. Sections: 392, 397, 379 IPC. Alert issued to all checkpoints.

FIR No. 014/2024 dated 28-04-2024. PS Medical College, District Meerut. Complainant: Station House Officer (suo motu). On 27-04-2024 at 2200 hours, during a raid at a godown in Shastri Nagar, Meerut, police team recovered 15 kg of smack (heroin) valued at approximately Rs. 30 crore in international market, 5 country-made pistols with 20 live cartridges, Rs. 8,50,000 cash, 12 mobile phones, and documents revealing a drug distribution network. Arrested: (1) Shakeel Ahmed alias Kalu, age 35, S/o Shri Jameel Ahmed, R/o Lisari Gate, Meerut — the kingpin, (2) Wasim Khan, age 28, R/o Sadar Bazaar, Meerut, (3) Firoz alias Firu, age 22, R/o Abu Lane, Meerut. Investigation reveals this network supplies heroin smuggled from the Nepal border through Gorakhpur-Lucknow-Meerut route. Shakeel has 7 prior NDPS cases across UP. Connection established with Varanasi drug network (ref FIR/2024/VN/008). Sections: 21, 22, 29 NDPS Act, 25 Arms Act, 120B IPC.

FIR No. 015/2024 dated 05-05-2024. PS Sadar, District Agra. Complainant: Smt. Kamla Devi, age 55 years, W/o Shri Babu Lal, R/o Lohamandi, Agra. The complainant reports that her granddaughter Anita (age 13, name changed) has been missing since 03-05-2024. The minor was last seen leaving for tuition classes at Shahganj area. Investigations reveal that one Raju alias Chhotu, age approximately 22 years, who has been previously reported in FIR/2024/AG/006 (Tajganj PS) for kidnapping, was seen near the tuition center. The accused has a pattern of targeting minor girls near educational institutions. He uses social media (Instagram and Snapchat) to befriend victims before luring them. Mobile tower location analysis shows the accused's phone was in the Shahganj area on the day of disappearance. Sections: 363, 366A IPC, Sec 5/6 POCSO Act. State-wide alert issued for the accused. Connection with FIR/2024/AG/006 confirmed — same accused, same MO.

FIR No. 016/2024 dated 12-05-2024. PS Gwaltoli, District Kanpur. Complainant: Shri Pankaj Agarwal, age 45 years, S/o Shri Suresh Agarwal, R/o Civil Lines, Kanpur. The complainant reports burglary at his jewelry shop 'Agarwal Jewellers' at Birhana Road on the night of 11-05-2024. Accused entered by cutting the rear wall and dismantled the alarm system. Stolen: gold jewelry (2.5 kg, value Rs. 1.25 crore), diamond sets (value Rs. 45 lakh), cash Rs. 3,50,000. Total loss approximately Rs. 1.73 crore. MO matches the Kanpur commercial burglary pattern — gas cutter entry, CCTV/DVR removed, early morning hours (estimated 0100-0400), and a white Eeco van spotted by a milk vendor at 0330 hours near the shop. This is the third such burglary in Kanpur in 3 months (ref FIR/2024/KN/003, FIR/2024/KN/004). Fingerprints recovered from the scene match latent prints from previous burglary at Swaroop Nagar. Sections: 457, 380, 411, 120B IPC. Special team constituted.

FIR No. 017/2024 dated 20-05-2024. PS Sigra, District Varanasi. Complainant: Shri Sudhir Srivastava, age 50 years, S/o Late Shri Hari Shankar Srivastava, R/o Sigra, Varanasi. The complainant reports that his wife Smt. Asha Srivastava (age 47) was murdered at their residence on 19-05-2024. The victim was found dead with multiple stab wounds in the bedroom at approximately 1900 hours. The domestic help Ramkali (age 35) found the body and alerted neighbors. Investigation reveals signs of forced entry through the kitchen window. Jewelry and cash are missing from the bedroom almari. Preliminary suspicion on the victim's nephew Sanjay Dubey, age 30, who had a property dispute with the family and was seen near the house at 1600 hours. CCTV footage from neighboring house shows an unidentified male entering through the rear gate at 1530 hours. Forensic team has collected blood samples, fingerprints, and DNA evidence. Sections: 302, 394, 449 IPC. Post-mortem report awaited.

FIR No. 018/2024 dated 28-05-2024. PS Kydganj, District Prayagraj. Complainant: Shri Yogesh Tripathi, age 38 years, S/o Shri Narayan Tripathi, R/o Teliarganj, Prayagraj. Complainant reports receiving extortion calls from the Munna Bhai gang demanding Rs. 5,00,000 for his construction material business. When he refused, his warehouse was set on fire on 27-05-2024 at approximately 0300 hours, causing damage estimated at Rs. 25,00,000. Two unidentified persons were seen on CCTV pouring inflammable liquid near the warehouse gate. The extortion pattern matches cases reported in Varanasi (FIR/2024/VN/007) and Prayagraj (FIR/2024/PR/012) — the 'Munna Bhai' name is used as a terror brand by the gang. Investigation reveals the gang leader is Munna alias Mohammad Shahid, age 34, R/o Naini, Prayagraj, with 12 prior cases including extortion, murder attempt, and arms act. Sections: 384, 435, 436, 506, 120B IPC. Arson investigation team deployed.

FIR No. 019/2024 dated 05-06-2024. PS Kotwali, District Meerut. Complainant: Smt. Rani Devi, age 68 years, W/o Late Shri Sukhdev, R/o Shastri Nagar, Meerut. The complainant reports that she received a WhatsApp call from a person claiming to be 'Vikram Sharma from RBI' who said her bank account had been flagged for money laundering and an arrest warrant had been issued. The caller put her on a fake 'police video call' where another person in uniform threatened her with arrest. Under extreme duress, she transferred Rs. 12,50,000 from her fixed deposit to accounts specified by the accused. The digital arrest scam is a known tactic of the Jamtara cyber fraud network. Same alias 'Vikram Sharma' used in FIR/2024/AG/005 and FIR/2024/GK/010. Money trail traced to accounts in Jamtara and Deoghar, Jharkhand. Sections: 384, 420, 170 IPC, 66C, 66D IT Act 2000. Joint investigation with Jharkhand police initiated.

FIR No. 020/2024 dated 15-06-2024. PS Aliganj, District Lucknow. Complainant: Station House Officer, Aliganj PS (suo motu). Based on intelligence inputs, a raid was conducted at a house in Sector-J, Aliganj, Lucknow on 14-06-2024. Recovered: 500 grams of MDMA (Ecstasy), 2 kg of ganja, drug paraphernalia including weighing scale and packaging material, Rs. 4,50,000 cash, and a list of 50+ customers. Arrested: (1) Sunny alias Sunny Yadav, age 26, S/o Shri Raj Kumar Yadav, R/o Aliganj, Lucknow — the local distributor, (2) Deepak alias Deepu, age 22, R/o Thakurganj, Lucknow — the peddler. Sunny's phone records reveal contacts with Shakeel Ahmed alias Kalu (arrested in FIR/2024/MR/014, Meerut) and Guddu Khan (arrested in FIR/2024/VN/008, Varanasi). This confirms the Nepal-Gorakhpur-Lucknow-Meerut drug supply chain. Deepak is the same 'Deepu' associated with Bablu's snatching gang at Thakurganj. Sections: 20, 22, 29 NDPS Act, 120B IPC.

FIR No. 021/2024 dated 22-06-2024. PS Cantt, District Gorakhpur. Complainant: Shri Ravi Shankar Pandey, age 58 years, S/o Late Shri Vishwanath Pandey, R/o Basharatpur, Gorakhpur. The complainant reports a case of dacoity. On 21-06-2024 at approximately 2130 hours, a group of 5 armed persons entered his house, held the family at gunpoint, and looted gold jewelry (500 grams, value Rs. 25,00,000), cash Rs. 5,00,000, and a licensed double-barrel gun. The gang leader was identified as Chhote Lal alias Chhotu (same accused as FIR/2024/GK/009) — recognized by the scar on his left cheek. Gang members arrived in an autorickshaw and two motorcycles. The complainant's son was pistol-whipped and sustained head injuries. This is the second armed crime by Chhote Lal in Gorakhpur within 3 months. He appears to be escalating from robbery to dacoity. Sections: 395, 397, 398, 25 Arms Act. State-wide alert for Chhote Lal issued.

FIR No. 022/2024 dated 30-06-2024. PS Charbagh, District Lucknow. Complainant: Shri Prabhat Sinha, age 30 years, S/o Shri Rajendra Sinha, R/o Rajajipuram, Lucknow. The complainant reports that on 29-06-2024 at approximately 2200 hours, near Charbagh bus stand, two bike-borne assailants snatched his laptop bag containing a Dell laptop (value Rs. 85,000), official documents, and Rs. 12,000 cash. The accused were on a black Pulsar motorcycle, one wearing a black hoodie — matching the chain snatching gang led by Bablu alias Bhura. The same gang has been linked to FIR/2024/LC/001, FIR/2024/LC/002, and FIR/2024/LC/013 operating in the Charbagh-Hazratganj corridor. Total estimated cases linked to this gang: 15+ in 6 months. The gang operates between 2100-0000 hours targeting lone pedestrians near railway station and major intersections. Sections: 356, 379 IPC. CCTV footage confirms Pulsar motorcycle with no plate.

FIR No. 023/2024 dated 08-07-2024. PS Chakeri, District Kanpur. Complainant: Shri Vijay Kumar, age 50 years, S/o Shri Ram Prasad, R/o Chakeri, Kanpur. The complainant reports that his mobile repair shop was burgled on the night of 07-07-2024. Entry was made by cutting the shutter with a gas cutter. Stolen: 30 mobile phones (value Rs. 6,00,000), repair equipment (value Rs. 2,00,000), cash Rs. 30,000. MO is identical to the Kanpur burglary gang — gas cutter on shutter, CCTV removed, night hours, white Eeco van. This is the 4th such burglary in Kanpur district (ref FIR/2024/KN/003, FIR/2024/KN/004, FIR/2024/KN/016). Forensic analysis of tool marks confirms the same cutting tool used across all cases. Suspected gang leader identified through informer as Pappu Kallu alias Kallu, age 38, R/o Barra, Kanpur, with 9 prior burglary cases. Sections: 457, 380, 411, 120B IPC.

FIR No. 024/2024 dated 15-07-2024. PS Lanka, District Varanasi. Complainant: Shri Ashok Mehta, age 44 years, S/o Shri Govind Mehta, R/o Lanka, Varanasi. The complainant reports that his handicraft showroom near Varanasi Cantt was attacked on 14-07-2024. Two persons entered posing as tourists, sprayed pepper spray on the staff, and looted gold-plated artifacts worth Rs. 8,00,000, cash Rs. 1,20,000, and the CCTV DVR. However, a hidden backup camera captured footage. The accused were identified as associates of the Munna Bhai extortion gang. Complainant had previously refused to pay protection money. This is a revenge attack. The gang's operations now span Varanasi (FIR/2024/VN/007), Prayagraj (FIR/2024/PR/012, FIR/2024/PR/018), and are expanding. Gang uses terror tactics — first extortion calls, then assault, then arson/robbery on refusal. Sections: 392, 384, 506, 120B, 328 IPC. Combined task force recommended.

FIR No. 025/2024 dated 22-07-2024. PS Cyber Crime, District Agra. Complainant: Shri Dinesh Sharma, age 45 years, Manager, Punjab National Bank, Sadar Branch, Agra. The bank reports that 23 customers have been defrauded through identical KYC-expiry phishing calls over a period of 3 months. Total fraud amount: Rs. 52,00,000. All cases share the same MO: caller claims to be from bank, creates urgency about KYC expiry or account blocking, obtains OTP, and makes rapid multiple transactions. Analysis of money trails shows all funds routed through the same set of 8 mule accounts. Investigation confirms this is the Jamtara-based network using the alias 'Vikram Sharma' (ref FIR/2024/AG/005, FIR/2024/GK/010, FIR/2024/MR/019). The network has defrauded victims across UP to the tune of Rs. 2+ crore. 4 mule account holders identified in Agra. Sections: 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B IPC, 66C, 66D IT Act 2000. Coordinated raids with Jharkhand Cyber Cell planned.
